utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. For the Prosecution Douglas Stringer, Lisa Biersay, Thomas Laugel, and legal intern, Kai Hong Leung.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic and Christopher Gosnell. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have two short oral rulings. The Trial Chamber was seized for the Prosecution's eleventh motion for leave to amend the Rule 65 ter exhibit list filed 21st of May. The Defence has indicated that it does not oppose the motion. The motion to amend is hereby granted and the Registry shall take the necessary measures to implement this decision. \ We are also seized of a confidential Prosecution request for substitution of documents included in the Rule 65 ter package of Witness GH-060 filed on 6th of May. The Defence has indicated that it takes no position in relation to the request. The request is hereby granted and the Registry shall take the necessary measures to implement this decision. The witness may be brought in. Perhaps it would be good to let the parties know and everyone know that we will take our second break at 12.00 rather than at 12.15 and it will be for half an hour and then we go on as usual. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness. I take it your testimony will be in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us your name and your date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name Morten Torkildsen. I was born on 4th June, 1965.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You are about to make the solemn declaration by which witnesses commit themselves to tell the truth. I have to point out to you that by doing so you -- you could be liable for perjury should you give false or untruthful information to the Tribunal. So could I now ask you to read the solemn declaration the Court Usher will give you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Torkildsen. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I can hear you very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Where do you currently call home, what country?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Norway.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Before we begin, if I may ask for some assistance in providing this binder of some selected documents to Mr. Torkildsen, and I have spoken to the Defence about it already. Thank you. It's just to get prepared for the documents that we'll go through.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Before we get to that, Mr. Torkildsen, could you tell the Trial Chamber where you were working between 2001 and 2003?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I worked here at the Office of the Prosecutor as a financial investigator.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What were your primary duties?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, for the first six months I was here in the first half of 2001. I was working asset tracing in relation to the Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did that task evolve into another?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. That -- after Mr. Milosevic was brought into custody in -- in the summer of 2001, I was tasked to -- to -- well, what I'm here for -- for today in terms of trying to identify whether there were any evidence regarding how Republika Srpska Krajina and Republika Srpska was financed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now we'll talk about that in more detail in a minute, but before we do that could you describe to the Trial Chamber where you worked immediately before joining the ICTY, specifically the Office of the Prosecutor, in 2001?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I was working for Advokatfirmaet in Norway which is the Norwegian service field office.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I was working as a financial investigator.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What were your duties there?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: My duties were to investigate cases involving allegations of fraud, corruption, and other financial irregularities.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you tell us how that pre-Tribunal experience assisted you in discharging your duties here when you worked at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It was to a large extent the same kind of work. I was identifying financial evidence. I was analysing that evidence, putting it into reports, and I was also occasionally testifying in court.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What is your educational background?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I am educated from the UK with a bachelor degree in management sciences from University of Manchester Institute of Science and Technology, department of management sciences, that was for my bachelor degree, and I'm also educated with a master of science from City University Business School in shipping, trade, and finance, mainly finance, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to focus now on your experience before international courts. In what cases have you testified before this Tribunal at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I have testified as an expert witness on finance in the Milosevic case and I also testified as an expert case in finance in the Perisic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What written evidence, if any, did you provide in those cases?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I provided in -- well, in the first -- in the Milosevic case I provided evidence regarding how both the Serbian controlled districts in Croatia and the Serbian controlled districts in Bosnia-Herzegovina were financed from the FRY -- FRY and from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when you describe that you provided evidence in this regard, was it in a report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Before what other international court have you appeared?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I've also appeared before the International Court of Justice here in The Hague as part of the team pleading the case of Bosnia-Herzegovina against Serbia and Montenegro. That was in 2006. I was then delivering or pleading the financial part of that case.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now turning to tab 92, may we please have 65 ter number 6423 displayed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you should also have that in your binder, but there is no need to turn to it. It's one -- two pages. And there is no B/C/S for this document. Do you recognise the document, Mr. Torkildsen?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Do you think you can have this enlarged?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, I forgot my glasses. Yes, I recognise this as my current CV.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And does it have the most up-to-date information regarding your professional experience?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 6423.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1974. Thank you. And just to mention there is B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, before we begin, could you describe for the Trial Chamber what the guiding principle is when you're conducting financial investigations?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, first of all, it's a matter of what your tasking is. And then it's a matter of trying to identify relevant documents according to your tasking. And that would be the first stage, then to try and identify documents. And then the second stage would be to try and collect these documents. And then I would conduct a review of the documents, an initial review. And then I would analyse them further. And normally in the end I would write up a report of my views on those documents and what they mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to go back to what you said, that initially when you joined the Office of the Prosecutor your task was to look into -- to trace the assets to the accused Milosevic and that changed. How did your assignment change?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, the -- the asset tracing is very much when the suspect is not in the control of -- or not in -- in custody. It's a matter of tracing assets to avoid, well, the flight risk of the suspect which is very much different from -- from this -- the work that I did later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The work -- how did you come to do the work that you did later on, specifically the collection of the documents that pertained to your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: During my asset tracing period, to put it like that, that lasted for, well, five or six months, I did when I looked into the huge collection of evidence that the OTP did discover that there were a lot of documents already at the OTP that could say something about how the RSK and the RS was financed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Were you formally asked to produce a report in this regard?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Not -- not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And eventually you were --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- asked? And what methodology did you undertake to produce this report that is the subject of your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I used the same methodology as I just described. I was concentrating on the -- on what was already in evidence at -- at the OTP, and then I'm talking about what's in the huge electronic evidence collection that's contained within the OTP. So I was simply trying to identify all documents that could be of relevance regarding how the Serb controlled districts in Croatia and the Serb controlled districts in Bosnia were financed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: How did you go about assessing the electronic data that was within the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, typically we would do electronic searches on key words like "banking," "finance," "money," "budgets," "accounts," et cetera, and I was again reviewing the hits together with of course a language assistant.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Are you able to quantify the pages of data that you reviewed during this process?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, there must have been thousands of -- of pages of documents. I -- most likely I spent a year trying to -- to identify documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When it came time -- I'm sorry. After you collected the documents, what did you then do?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, I reviewed them in -- in much more detail doing an analysis and see -- and try to see whether there were any kind of pattern when it comes to the financing.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And were you able to discern a pattern in the financing of the RSK and the RS?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. It was pretty clear. And it was -- well, both the RS and the RSK, it was financed in the -- in the same manner. Both of those entities were more or less exclusively financed from -- from Belgrade, at least for a -- for a certain period.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like now to turn to tab 48, which is 65 ter 2477.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And that's also in your binder, Mr. Torkildsen. Is it -- regarding your glasses, is it easier for you to see the screen or is it easier to work with a hard copy? Just to know how to go forward.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I think I'll manage with the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: As long as you can direct me to the right tab number.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, your glasses are at the hotel or are they at the witness room here in the building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. I think I forgot them at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I'll manage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I have a pair if we are in dire need that I can lend you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So if we could now have 65 ter 2477.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Which is tab 48 for you, Mr. Torkildsen. I'm just waiting for it to come on the screen. Looking at the first page of this document, do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise this as the report I wrote at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I know we are looking at the first page at the table of contents. Could you just briefly describe in your own words how you approached the organisation of the report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, my tasking, then, was to -- to try and identify if any relevant documents regarding how the RSK and how Republika Srpska was financed from -- from institutions in the FRY and the Republic of Serbia under the alleged control of Slobodan Milosevic. That was my tasking. And again my methodology was according to what I have described previously.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And as far as the structure of the report, how did you approach that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. I was tasked to divide the documents into the financing of the Serb controlled districts in Croatia in one section and another section regarding the financing of -- of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The problem being with that was that both these two entities were financed in the same manner, so it was difficult for me to sort of put, well, one document in -- in an -- in one box because the pattern of financing were -- were exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Generally speaking, how are the expenses of a country financed?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Normally countries are financed by -- by taxes, like taxes on personal income, VAT, taxes on business profits, custom duties, government borrowing, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And in the period before 1991, how were the expenses within Yugoslavia financed?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: They were mostly financed from what I described just now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Briefly, could you describe the different levels of budgets that existed in -- in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well from the time-period that I looked at then, mainly 1991 to and including 1995, I have reviewed budgets and annual accounts of the SFRY, the FRY, Republika Srpska, Republika Srpska Krajina, and also some of the SAOs in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Going back to your description about how financing typically works in countries, do you have a term when you talk about the taxes and those components that you previously described?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. In the -- the budgets and accounts that I have reviewed, the typical term for this would be "original income." And "original income" in this respect means -- means taxes, VAT, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: How did the financing evolve in the former Yugoslavia from what you've just described as the original income?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: What I have seen from the -- from the early budgets and accounts that I reviewed, then talking about 1991, it was to -- then early in 1991, yeah, it was to a large extent financed by what I now have described as original income. But then later on in the second half of 1991, the budgets started to be financed by the National Bank of Yugoslavia through the printing of money at the printing facility in Belgrade under the control of the National Bank of Yugoslavia. So were -- so the SFRY in the second half of 1991 were to an escalating sort of progression from this finance of the printing of money.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What conclusions did you reach regarding the source of financial and material support relied upon by the Serb controlled districts in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina from 1991 into -- for purposes of your report until 1995?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it -- it started in -- in 1991 where the Serbian Ministry of Defence were providing material sources and financial sources to the Serb controlled districts in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What was the basis for your conclusion in this regard?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Quite a few documents. There were communication letters and official notes from -- from meetings between the leadership of Serbia and the leadership of the Serb controlled districts in Croatia, and I also reviewed requests from the Serb controlled districts in -- in Croatia in late 1991 and responses to that from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what conclusions, if any, did you reach regarding the source of financing for the Army of the RSK and of the Republika Srpska, the RS?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: When we are moving into 1992, the National Bank of Yugoslavia were printing money on an escalated basis and that money was used to finance the budget deficits of both Republika Srpska Krajina and Republika Srpska -- that was one part of the financing - and the budgetary financing from Belgrade to these two entities; and you also have the -- the case that -- that the FRY financed the offices of the RS Army and the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What was the basis for that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: The financing of the offices, again, that is apparent from the document that I have reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The printing of money, does that -- or are there some terms that are used to describe that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. There are various terms. And those terms are apparent from the budgets and annual accounts that I have reviewed. You have a term called "primary emissions," you have "primary issues," and you also have the term "credits," but they all basically mean money printed at the top cedar [phoen] mint, the printing facility of the National Bank of Yugoslavia in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to tab 13 which is in your binder, and it is 65 ter 568. Now, Mr. Torkildsen, I notice that you are reading it in your binder. Are you able to see --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- clearly?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I'm able to see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Good. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise it. That's one of the documents that I have reviewed for my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for the record this is referenced in paragraphs 25, 33, and 98 of your report. What do you recognise this document to be?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it is -- that is a statement there -- an official note from the talks between representatives of the RSK government and President Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And looking in the first paragraph, it describes who is present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. And it's -- it also refers to the meeting taking place on 12th November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could -- are you able to see the underlined names?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So we can have it in the record.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. The ones present were then-President Slobodan Milosevic; Prime Minister Radoman Bozovic; and the governor of the National Bank of Serbia; and from the RSK, it was President Goran Hadzic; Prime Minister Zecevic; and Minister of the Interior Martic; Minister of Defence Spanovic; and Finance Minister Peuraca; and Deputy Prime Minister Bosko Bozanic. And it is further stated here that at that meeting the mode of financial assistance to the Krajina until the end of this year was agreed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what significance, if any, did this document have for your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it had the significance that -- that the -- that the leadership of the RSK was discussing with the president of Serbia how they should be -- should be financed. And I also, well, compare -- and I also comparing this to other document -- documents that this is really a meeting where they are outlining their coming needs, financial needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention to the -- let's say the fourth paragraph, which is really the second substantial paragraph, and it's underlined: "The president, Mr. Milosevic, agreed to the concept of creating a defence system of the Krajina which would be based on about 23.000 people in the police, of whom 5.000 in the regular force and 18.000 in brigades which would make up the peacetime corps of the army and provide security for the borders of the Krajina." What relevance, if any, did that have for your findings in your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it outlines the size of the manpower that needs to be financed from Belgrade. And I would also like to highlight what is written further down in that paragraph. It was accepted that the planning of funds for army and police needs should be begin immediately as was done in 1992 via the RSK Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia. So what they also -- well, this document is telling me that they are also pointing back at the practice that had been going on for some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now like to leave this document and go to tab 38. And in tab 38 which is 65 ter number 1926, I'd first like you to look at the first page and then we'll move to page 20. But let's get first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And consistent with the Court's guidelines on exhibits cited in the expert report, we won't be tendering them individually in the courtroom which is why I didn't tender the previous one. And for the record this document is also referenced in paragraph 116 of the report. So if I could have just the first page so I could have Mr. Torkildsen identify it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Are you --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: This is one of the documents that I have reviewed for my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it is, as it is stated there on the first page, it is a memorandum for the co-ordination of tasks meeting at the Yugoslav Army General Staff on 17th December, 1993. It is also mentioned here in top right-hand corner that it is military secret and it's a strictly confidential document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now if we could move to page 20, which I believe is page 10 in the B/C/S but page 20 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And specifically under that subsection (c) entitled: "New Requests." Now this reads: "We have learned unofficially that of the above total balance of requirements for 1994, the federal government will only be able to provide USD 850 million for all three armed forces instead of USD 3.29 billion ..." And below it says: "For the SVK, this would amount to USD 79.3 million instead of USD 307.30 million." Could you describe what is being addressed in that section?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: What is being addressed here are the -- the requirements for the three armed forces at that time for -- for 1994. What I find interesting about this exact quotes here is the fact that they are referring to the numbers in dollar terms because this was at the time when -- when -- when the FRY and also the RSK and the RS were facing hyperinflation meaning that the dinar terms and the value of money at that time is -- is difficult to put into perspective. But here they are actually mentioning the amounts in US dollar terms. So it's easy to understand the value of the money. But that is one point. And the other point is that they are talking about the needs for all three armed forces together and they are talking about the federal government providing for all three armed forces, viewing them as -- as one, well - what can we say? - one collect army. At least they are looking at the financing for all three armies together.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now this refers to 1994. What relevance, if any, would it have for the period of 1991 to 1993 which is the time-period of the indictment in this case?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, from all the documents I've seen, the financing were the same for the -- also for the previous years.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now like to move, if we may, to tab 33 which is 65 -- excuse me, it's been previously admitted as Exhibit P208.140.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Also referenced in your report. Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. Again it's one of the documents I have previously reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it's -- it's a document signed by Minister Milan Martic of the RSK Ministry of the Interior in Knin, and it is addressed to the president of the Republic of Serbia, Mr. Slobodan Milosevic; the prime minister of the Republic of Serbia; and the minister of interior of the Republic of Serbia at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: And it is simply a request for money.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what significance did this have for your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: What I think is highly significant here, and it is pointed at the fact that I have seen from reviewing the budgets and the annual accounts, and that is what is written here in the third paragraph: "There are no funds in the budget of the RS Krajina for any significant increase as the RS Krajina has no real sources from which to fill its budget, as you certainly know." As I tried to explain earlier today is that a budget, a government budget, is normally financed through what I described as original income: Taxes, VAT, et cetera. But the RS Krajina at that time had no such income or at least not to -- to any large extent to finance its budget. And this is exactly what Milan Martic is pointing out there, that the RS Krajina has no real sources from which to fill its budget, "as you certainly know." And that's why he's addressing Mr. Milosevic and others in order to fill that budget.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when you say Mr. Milosevic, why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Because the -- this letter or request is addressed to him and to others.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn your attention to tab 23, if we may, which is previously admitted Exhibit P1311 which is also referenced in your report, paragraph 71. While we wait for it to be on the screen, do you recognise the document that I see that you are looking at in your binder?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this document as one of the documents I previously reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It is a request from the government of the RSK to the federal executive council -- federal secretariat for finance Yugoslav national bank and it's addressed to the governor and deputy governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia. It is stated at -- personally, them personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What significance, if any, did this have for your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I would like to -- to quote what this -- what this -- what is stated here. Well, first of all, they are referring to an article and so on. And then it is stated here, "... please pay the some of --" These numbers are very high, so they are sort of difficult to put it into context, but the way I see it: "... please pay the some of 12.900.000.000 dinars, the funds required for July, to the budget of the Republic of Srpska Krajina no later than 29th June 1992." So the government of the RSK here is requesting the National Bank of Yugoslavia to pay for their needs to -- to fulfil the income side of their budget for July 1992, and it also then points that the instrumental and important role that the National Bank of Yugoslavia is providing in terms of providing financing for the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now, if I may, move to tab 1 which is 65 ter 208.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for it electronically, in your binder do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, again, I recognise this as one of the documents I have reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for the record, it's referenced in paragraph 18 of your report. Just based on the first page, what do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it is a document by the federal executive council and it is a proposal of minimal needed funds that need to be provided in the budget of the Federation for the period July to September 1991. And it is dated Belgrade, 21st July 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What significance, if any, did the -- the numbers on page 2 of this exhibit have for you regarding your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, first of all, I would like to mention that -- or just state that this a budget for that period for the SFRY. And on page 2 it is -- it is stated what the money in that budget should be spent on, used for.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: And the -- the total expenses here are listed at the bottom under the total figure as -- as 26.7 -- approximately 26.7 billion dollars -- no, not dollars, dinars, sorry. And we can see from the top here that out of that total amount of -- of 26.7 billion dinars we can see that 17.7 billion dinars are going for the JNA, the army. So approximately two-thirds of the expenditure in this budget is suggested to go for the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we could now move to the next page, please, being page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What I'd like to focus on is in the -- towards the end, the words "original income," and on the far right side it says 42.4. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you describe what that is?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, that is the percentage of income originating from what I had described previously as original income, the taxes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And -- but below that there is the number 52.3. Could you describe what that number is associated with?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. That is the percentage being financed by the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what type of financing is that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, that is -- at this time it is either a loan to the government budget by the National Bank of Yugoslavia or it would be a primary emissions, the printing of money. But -- but as we have seen later on, whether you gave a loan at that time or whether you just provided funds to the -- to the printing of money, that would be the same thing because -- because of the hyperinflation, that means that if you gave someone a loan, they would virtually need to pay back nothing because the money in just a few months later be would be worth almost nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I would like now to turn your attention to tab 4, which is also referenced in your report at paragraph 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And this is 65 ter number 265.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And my question to you while we wait for the electronic version to be brought up is: Do you recognise this document and, if so, what do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Again, I have reviewed this document before. It's a document by the federal executive council, and it's a draft law on revenue sources for financing certain national defence requirements in 1991. And it is dated September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for our purposes, if we could please go to page 6, which I believe is B/C/S 5. And if we could scroll down in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now like to direct your attention to the paragraph that begins: "Of the total funds of 22.500 million dinars approved by the Yugoslav national bank, 15.700 million dinars familiars have been used for financing the JNA and a some of 6.800 million dinars has been used for settling obligations under sub-balances for financing other functions as below ..." And it follows there as a heading for the JNA. Could you describe what relevance, if any, this had for your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, this draft law is basically about how the JNA should be -- should be financed from -- from this point in time and onwards. And it is clearly stated that it's going to be financed from the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: And I'd also like to draw to your attention the -- the following page and the first paragraph on -- on that page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So if we could now move to page 7 which is still, I believe, B/C/S 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Is it the paragraph that begins, "Due to an insufficient --"

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: So that is supporting what I have described earlier on. It is stated here, "Due to the insufficient inflow of revenue, problems in financing the JNA have reached a critical point." As I have tried to explain, there were a lack of original income at that time and, therefore, they had to find an alternative way of financing the JNA and the result was the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now this pertains to paragraph 20 of your report and at this time I would like to look at your report which is tab 48, and specifically on page 7, paragraph 19. And it's regarding a -- a name that may be incorrectly attributed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could we please have page 7 of 65 ter -- of tab 48, which is 65 ter 2477, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now this actually -- we won't be discussing in detail that exhibit, but it -- in that paragraph 19, you are referring, I believe, to our 65 ter 253. Now this is your report and I'll bring your attention to page 7 where we see the name "Slobodan Pelivan." And then below we come to "Jure Pelivan." Is -- or were those the correct names reflected in the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember. But it should -- the first name, "Slobodan Pelivan" should read "Jure Pelivan." That is his correct name. But as far as I remember, it was -- it must have been a typo then in the -- in the B/C/S original version.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now if we may turn to tab 22 which is 65 ter 1143. And in that regard, you were able to review some translations that differed slightly from the quotes that you actually had in your report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. There do exist many various translations of the same documents within the OTP, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And did those minor changes in the translations change your reliance on the documentation in any way?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No. The core essence of the documents were the same any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And so now if we could turn to this tab 22, 65 ter number 1134. Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen and reviewed the document before.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for the record this is in your report at paragraphs 25, 62, and 73. What is this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, this document is a publication in the Official Gazette of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it is dated the 8th June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what relevance, if any, did this have for your report? And perhaps it -- it would be -- can you use the version that's on the screen before you, if you can see it, because I think your binder may not have the most up-to-date version.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, correct. I do not have this in my binder. It is a decision on the use of funds from primary issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do I need to have that enlarged for you or can you read it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: If you can enlarge it a bit, that would be great. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Okay. And what relevance if any did this have for your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, I would like to read out what is written there in Article 1: "Funds from the national bank of Yugoslavia's primary issue shall be used in accordance with the Decision of the National Bank of Yugoslavia on the goals and tasks of the common monetary policy and common elements of the credit policy in 1992, pursuant to the conditions stipulated in this Decision." It is, well, to put it in a simple manner, it is stated here that -- sorry, now I've got the B/C/S version in front of me. It is stated here that it's up to the National Bank of Yugoslavia to decide how this money that has been sent to the Republika Srpska should be used.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what did that mean to you in terms of your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it -- it -- it means to me that it is Belgrade who's determining the use of the money. I would also like to draw your attention to a matter that is also important and that is Article 3 in this decision. It is stated here that: "Primary issue funds," meaning again the printing of money from Belgrade, "shall be transferred temporarily to the accounts of commercial banks for certain purposes through a special account of the payment transactions and auditing services ..." And I would like to pay to your attention the payment, transaction, and auditing service which was an important instrument in having money transported from Belgrade and distributed to the RS and the RSK during 1991, 1992, 1993, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What is the SDK?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it's -- it's -- it's basically a mechanism for transferring money. Just as we do have a functioning banking system today, we can -- we can -- we can, well, get money across borders. I mean, it's like compare it to the banking SWIFT system that we have functioning in Western Europe and other places in the world today.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is the relationship, if any, between the SDK that you've just described and this payment, transactions, and auditing service?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is the same. It's just various translations of the SDK that do exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to tab 75 which is a document that's not in your report, and it's 65 ter 1655. I've -- in paragraph 116 of your report, you describe the FRY financing of the RSK and the RS, and I'd like to direct your attention to this document. Have you had a chance to review this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, there -- it is the minutes or the shorthand notes of a session of the Supreme Defence Council held on 2nd June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to go to the second page of the document which in the B/C/S it's between pages 1 and 2. I think the last paragraph gets split. But in the English it's the very top paragraph of page 2. Actually, could we go back to page 1 just briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I don't want to go into details about the -- all the attendees, but it may be useful just to point out a few. According to this, Slobodan Milosevic, president of Serbia, is present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: As well as Colonel-General Zivota Panic, the Chief of General Staff of th Yugoslav Army. Is that listed is there as well?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now I'd like to go to page 2 of the English. And it discusses that the Supreme Defence Council discussed the financial situation of the Yugoslav Army at the time of the passing of the budget and then again after the budget for -- for 1993 was passed, and also the federal government discussed it together with the governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia. What, if anything, of significance does that hold for you and your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, first of all, if possible, I would like to take you back to the -- to the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: On page 1?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. Because there is a heading here for that topic they are discussing.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And towards the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. It is -- it is stated there that the topic for their discussion is "information on problems regarding the funding of the Yugoslav Army."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now directing your attention to the second page to the section that I read, and my question was: What significance, if any, that had for you --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, there is --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- in terms of your report, of course?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, the significance is that information that is actually contained within this document corroborates -- well, other documents that I have seen at the time that I -- I -- I wrote my report. And they are discussing the financial situation of the Yugoslav Army at that time, and it also important to note this that it is stated here that the federal government discussed it together with the governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia. And that is natural, considering that the National Bank of Yugoslavia was so instrumental in financing the army at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now I'd like to move to page 8 of the English which I believe is also page 8 of the B/C/S, and I'm focusing on what's attributed to Radoje Kontic. I just want the verification that it is Radoje Kontic. And if we could now move to the next page in the English and also the next page in the B/C/S which would now be page 9. And I'd like to direct your attention to the paragraph that begins "What is going on with the Federation budget?" At the very end of page 9 in the English. Now it continues: "You know that we do not have any import or export. Our basic direct revenues are customs and turnover taxes, and yet there are almost no customs, revenues." And it continues. I'd like to skip down a couple of lines. And it reads: "Since the turnover is in decline, our revenues are in decline too. In this way, the federal budget is de facto in the same situation as in the first half of the last year - when it was exclusively financed from the primary issue." What significance, if any, does that statement have for your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, this statement from Radoje Kontic simply confirms in plain language what I have stated in my report. He's saying that they do not have any original income. He's pointing then at the lack of custom revenue. And he's stating that they exclusively have to rely on primary issues, again the money coming from the National Bank of Yugoslavia. And it's also important to note that he's pointing back in time saying that that was also the same situation in the first half of last year, meaning 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time the Prosecution would seek to tender 65 ter 1655 which is not part of Mr. Torkildsen's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P1975. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Similarly, tab 79 which is next one in your binder is not part of your report. And it is 65 ter 2125. I'd also like you to take a look at that. While we wait for the electronic version, have you reviewed this document before?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it is the final accounts of the federal budget for 1993 and it is -- it was published in the Official Gazette of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia on 10th March 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you briefly tell us what is the difference between an account and a budget?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, a budget is a plan of income and expenses. Accounts are what actually took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And generally speaking, I'll take you to some figures shortly, what relevance if any did this have for your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: First -- first of all, I would like to bring to your attention the -- the -- well, to put it like that, the ridiculous high numbers that are listed in the accounts. This was at the time of hyperinflation that had been going on for quite some time, so it's difficult to interpreter the numbers as such. What is important regarding the numbers here is that you must view them, well, compared to each other, meaning that you must review the different lines, how much in percentage-wise is going to the army, how much is coming from primary emissions and so on. But as we can read here from the first page is that the -- the total generated income in this -- in this annual accounts for 1993 is -- is 25.864-something. I'm not going to even try to spell out the -- the figures because here you can see that it's also listed in millions of dinars, meaning that you can actually put six zeros behind this number. But you see the total income.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And perhaps I can direct your attention to 09-5 on the -- on the left-hand side of page -- of the second page.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. 09-5, that line is describing where the income is coming from. And it is stated here that -- that 25.552-something is coming from the National Bank of Yugoslavia. It says here credits from the National Bank of Yugoslavia. That means the primary emissions. And if you compared that figure 25.552-something to the total amount on the first page, which is 25.864, that means that virtually all of the income in this annual accounts is coming from the National Bank of Yugoslavia. So the total income side is derived from the printing of money.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At the bottom of that page and continuing on to page 3, there is a heading: "General purpose 02 the Yugoslav Army." What relevance, if any, does that section have for your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it -- it states how the money is spent, and it is stated that 22.588-something is being spent on the Yugoslav Army --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Torkildsen, you're reading the "general purpose" double line at the -- almost at the bottom; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: And again, comparing that figure of 22.588 to the total income side of 25.864, out from that I have drawn the conclusion that -- that most of the income in this annual accounts is being spent on the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 2125 which is not contained in Mr. Torkildsen's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P1976. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to turn to yet another document that's not in our report and that is tab -- can be found at tab 66. And it's been previously admitted as Exhibit P1903. Have you been able to read -- review this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It is, again, the shorthand notes from one of these sessions of the Supreme Defence Council. This one was held on 10th February 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to page 2 which I believe is also B/C/S 2. Now again we have a list of attendees. But what I'd like to do is to focus your attention on the agenda item number 3.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. On the agenda is: "Information on problems related to financing of the Yugoslav Army and financing of the assistance to the Republic of Serbian Krajina." I'd just like to mention that I have reviewed quite a big number of minutes from the Supreme Defence Council, and the financing of the Yugoslav Army is often on the agenda of -- in the SDC meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If I may now take you to page 27 of the English, and I think it's B/C/S page 25. And it's under that heading: "Information about the problems related to the provision of funds for the Yugoslav Army and the provision of financial aid for the Republic of Serbian Krajina." And we have Zivota Panic speaking. If I could direct your attention to the -- after the first paragraph. Could you briefly summarise what's being discussed here by Panic?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, Zivota Panic, at that time, the -- the chief of the VJ, was -- is pointing at -- well, I can just quote here: "As for the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, huge amounts of material means have been sent to these areas." Further: "Whatever we send them, we have to refund at our market, no matter whether it's food, spare parts, ammunition, clothing, et cetera." He's simply here pointing at what the FRY have provided to the RS and the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now further down in the third paragraph it reads: "We have sent 700 commanding officers to the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina - they are still there, they are volunteers and they have come from those areas. We have prepared and armed 3.000 volunteers that we have sent to the Republic of Serbian Krajina." What significance, if any, did that section that we have just described have for your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, this is again a section that corroborates what I have written in my report, that the offices of the VRS army and the RS army are being financed from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now if I may take you to the next page just to see the speaker who continues on page 29, which will be my final focus. So on page 28 you will see Miodrag Dragojevic who is described on page 2 of this document being the assistant minister of defence for military and economy sector. And now if we could move from page 28 to the next page, being 29. I'd like to direct your attention to the middle of that page, specifically the paragraph that begins, "Apart from that ...," and down to the very bottom of the page. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now the -- that sentence: "Apart from that, we should de facto give 320 billion dinars from the primary emission from the first quarter --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay, one moment please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. I was just wondering if we could get to the proper page in the B/C/S before we proceed forward. I think it should be a couple of pages further along.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Page 27. Thank you. I think maybe one more page in the B/C/S, I think. Ah, okay, I do see the 320. I think this is the right page, but I'll be corrected if it's not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If we're looking at: "Apart from that, we should de facto give 320 billion dinars from the primary emission for the first quarter, which is for the needs of these two army branches ..." What significance, if any, do you attribute to the use of the word "branches"?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, he's, in my view, referring to the VJ and to the VRS, the Army of Republika Srpska. What is interesting here is that he's just, well, in my view, referring to two branches of the same army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now if we could go to the paragraph at the bottom that begins, "And on top of this ..."

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. What he's pointing at here is that not only do they have to cater for the needs of the VJ and the VRS, they also discuss the funding of the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Before we leave that page, could we please scroll up to the top of this B/C/S page. Now, in the B/C/S this is attributed to Radoje Kontic; is that correct? Do you see that on the screen before you? You'd have to look at the screen --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- because the B/C/S version isn't -- it's Radoje --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Okay. So this is a statement by Radoje Kontic and not by Miodrag Dragojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for that reason, Your Honours, at this time could we please have it MFI'd so we could take the time to correct the translation so the proper speaker is attributed to the section we've just discussed? So we would -- oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So we'll -- so we'll submit a revised -- a motion for substitution, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- because it's already admitted. So we'll leave it as is for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Do you see the time, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I do indeed, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Torkildsen, we will take the first break come back at 11.00. The Court Usher will escort you out of the court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Torkildsen. Yes, Ms. Biersay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I see that you have your glasses.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Okay. If I could now direct your attention to tab 91 which is 65 ter 6422, and this is not part of your report. Have you reviewed this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it is one of the shorthand notes and this one from the 17th session of the Supreme Defence Council held on 10th January 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now as usual, we have a list of attendees and directing your attention to the bottom of the page under the agenda, "Discussion of the funding for the Yugoslav Army," and what I'd like to do is go to the next page which I believe is also page 2 in B/C/S. And at the bottom of page 2 we see Momcilo Perisic speaking; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we could flip through pages 3 and 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could we have the next page in the English, please. I basically wanted to show that the speakers are remaining the same. And if we could go to the next page in the English, settling on page 5 in the English, which I believe is B/C/S 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, there are quite a few pages covering what is being said by Perisic, but what I'd like to focus on is the last two paragraphs above Slobodan Milosevic. The first full paragraph reads: "This means that 522 million dollars are needed for the Republika Srpska and 307 million dollars for the Republic of Serbian Krajina ..." And it continues: "... for the Yugoslav army," et cetera. But focusing on that first paragraph, what significance, if any, did it have for your findings in your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, again it corroborates the documents that I have reviewed as the basis for my report. This -- the amounts being referred to here is what is needed for Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina if the war will continue in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph it reads: "... just for comparison: In the course of the previous year, 437 million dollars were approved." What if anything of significance does that have for your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, the shorthand notes is here pointing back in time to what happened in 1993 where 437 million dollars were approved. And the way that I read this is that it was approved for the needs of the RS and the RSK during 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at this time we tender 65 ter 6422.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I can just add one comment to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: The figure here of 437 million dollars were approved, this is just a reference to the -- to the financial side of this. The direct -- in monetary terms. But also the next sentence there, it's pointed out "1.2 billion dollars that were spent from the materiel stockpiles are not taken into account here," so actually that figure comes in addition to the 437 million dollars.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at this time we would tender 65 ter 6422.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P1977. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn your attention to tab 27 which is previously admitted Exhibit P185, which is referenced at paragraph 97 of your report. What do you recognise this document to be?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it is one of the -- well, first of all, it is one of the documents that I reviewed for my report, and it is a request for funds from the Republic of Serbian Krajina Ministry of Defence to the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia, and it is addressed to the minister Negovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What significance, if any, did this have for your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, as I started with this morning, this is one of the requests coming from the RSK to the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia for financial and -- for financial support.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page in the English. It's just the one page in B/C/S. And we can scroll down on the B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And can you see the -- the name of the person signing this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Colonel Stojan Spanovic, Minister of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now turning our attention to tab 35, previously admitted Exhibit P209.140.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, am I able to make one more comment on this previous document?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you're referring to tab 27?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes. Please do.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: What I find, well, rather particular about this document is that they are talking about the -- the planned funds. So this is part of the plan. It is not a random request. That is clear from -- from the last paragraph on page -- on page 1. And also on the -- on the top of page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Which reads -- but we leave --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I will -- I will read it out.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: "Therefore we ask you to transfer to us the planned funds of approximately 200 million per month, otherwise it will be impossible to maintain the whole system we have created. We know that the financial difficulties you are facing, but we believe that you will find a way to provide these funds especially as they are not outside the total planned quota."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And the second part of that is on the following page. Yes. Thank you. Is there anything else regarding this document that you would like to highlight?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now if we could turn to tab 35, again, previously admitted Exhibit 209.140 referenced in your report at paragraph 102. What do you recognise this document to be?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it is a letter from the Republic of Srpska Krajina, the cabinet of the president from -- more specifically from the president of the republic, Mr. Goran Hadzic, and it is addressed to the president of the Republic of Serbia, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you direct us to the portions of this letter that you considered relevant for purposes of your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, when I brought the report, that was a report that was to be in -- in connection with the Milosevic case, and, of course, this is a direct request from the president of the RSK at that time directly to Mr. Milosevic requesting funds or his assistance in -- in acquiring funds for the use of the RSK. And in particular in that third paragraph Mr. Hadzic is pointing out they need help regarding technical maintenance of weapons and acquisitions of ammunition, et cetera. And in the last sentence he's pointing out: "We are not financially in position to make up for medium and general service which may be done by the institutions of the Yugoslav Army." They are, well, he's simply pointing out the lack of funds they have themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we skip the next paragraph and go to the following one that begins: "Representatives of the SAK Headquarters together with their commandant presented these problems at the last meeting with the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army on 24 May, 1993," what significance if any does that have?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, the way that I read this is that these problems regarding financing and the need for materiel support has been discussed also previously.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: May we now turn to another tab. Now turning to tab 37 which is 65 -- which has been previously admitted as Exhibit P1314. And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: This is a document -- a letter from the Republic of Serbian Krajina, Ministry of the Interior to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia. And it concerns the transportation of cash from -- from -- from Belgrade to the RSK; more specifically, to Knin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Torkildsen, I'd like to move now from this tab, if that's okay, to tab 11, which is previously admitted Exhibit P1282, referenced at paragraphs 25, 33, 92, and 103 of your report. What do you recognise this document to be?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: This is a document or a letter than from the Republic of Serbia Ministry of Defence to the government of the Republic of Serbia. And it is dated 1st November 1991. And the subject of this letter is, "Report on providing assistance to Serbian districts in Croatia." And it is outlining the financial assistance needed for the -- for the period November and December 1991 regarding the needs of the territorial defence in Krajina SAO, Western Slavonia, and SO Slavonia, Baranja and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And specifically you're referring to the third paragraph on page 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. Where it's outlined that the financial assistance that should be provided for November and December 1991 amounts to 1.205 billion dinars at that time. And that should cover the needs of about 50.000 men of the Territorial Defence at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now also attached to this are some lists. I won't ask you to go through them but just to indicate that they are lists relating to specific items; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. These lists are detailing the -- what the financial and material support consists of.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, with your permission, I'd like to move to another tab; specifically, tab 61 which is not in your report, and it has been previously admitted as Exhibit P150. Have you been able to review this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It is a document providing information on the funds provided in the budget of the republic for the aid to the Serbian areas in Croatia with the proposal for the solutions of their realisation. This is -- this is a document corroborating the previous document that we -- that we discussed, the last one.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now the first sentence reads: "By the Conclusion of the Government of the Republic of Serbia ... and pursuant to the information on Providing aid to the Serbian Areas in Croatia, the funds in the amount of 1.260 million dinars have been appropriated to the Defence Ministry and transferred to the giro account, for position 49 of the Budget of the Republic of Serbia for the year 1991." Now in the next paragraph it references the plans for the mentioned funds for salaries, daily allowance, and other materiel rights for the months of November and December 1991, of about 49.300 members of the Territorial Defence of the SAO Krajina, Western Slavonia, and SO Slavonia, Baranja, Western Srem, in the amount of 1.179 million dinars. And how does this fit into the conclusions of your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it fits in with the conclusion in my report that -- that the Ministry of Defence of -- of -- of the Serb republic were providing financial assistance to the -- to the SAOs in Krajina. And also for this documents the figures there when it comes to finance and also the manpower that the members of the Territorial Defence, et cetera, the figures are almost the same as in -- in the previous document that we discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time I'd like to move to tab 8, which is previously admitted Exhibit P255.253.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And this is referenced in your report at paragraph 60. What do you recognise this document to be?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It is a decision signed by Mr. Goran Hadzic regarding opening of a bank account for the year -- for the budget of the Serbian region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And that is described just under the word "Decision" there. And could I direct your attention to what's under Roman numeral II.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. It is stated there that the purpose of opening this account is to finance the Serbian region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, and territories not included in the municipalities an account should be open under the name budget of Serbian region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: That's under --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, that was under I --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Roman numeral I. And now the Roman numeral II.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It is written here: "Budgetary revenues of Serbian region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem will be formed in accordance with current legal regulations of the FRY, Republic of Serbia, and Serbian region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, whereas disbursements will be made via municipalities of Beli Manastir administration."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And this is -- at the end it says: "In Dalj, 21 September 1991"; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now if I could direct your attention to tab 56 which is not in your report, and it's 65 ter 311. Have you been able to review this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have. Again, this is document is -- is a decision signed by Mr. Goran Hadzic and it concerns who has got the signatory rights on that -- that account that we discussed in the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And five people are listed under article 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Six --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me, six people.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: -- people.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And there is Mr. Goran Hadzic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And number two, Bogdan Vojnovic, Jovan Pejakovic, Vitomir Devetak, Boro Milinkovic, and Vojin Susa; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is the significance of Article 2?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it is just that in order to make transfers you need two signatories, and it is not just one person that can sign on his own.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honours, the Prosecution would seek to tender 65 ter 311.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P1978. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If I could now direct your attention to tab 9, which is previously admitted Exhibit P256.253, and this is referenced in your report at paragraph 59. What is this document that we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It is a document from the -- from the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Serbian region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, addressed to the public auditing service of Vojvodina. Again, as I pointed out earlier today, the public auditing service is the same as the SDK, the vehicle or the transfer mechanism that was used in order to transfer funds from one place to another. And it is a request for a opening a giro account regarding the budget of Serbian region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. This document should be read and interpreted together with the two previous documents that we have looked at, the signatory rights and -- and -- and the opening of the account document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now I have two more documents I'd like to show you. Neither one of them is in your report. And I estimate that will take about five to seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If I could now direct your attention to tab 71, which is 65 ter 1581.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Have you been able to review this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
