utterances.text: Well, the -- this document was published in the Official Gazette of the RSK on the 20th of May, 1992, and it is a decision on the budget of the Serbian district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem for the year 1992. So again pointing back at this is a budget, a plan for income and expenditure in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention to page 3 in the English which I believe is the B/C/S page 2. And I would like to go straight to the line that reads 780 on the left-hand side and it's listed under 1 for revenues beginning on page 2 and it continues on this page 3. Could you describe for us what we see at that block attributed to 780?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. At the bottom they are summing up. We can see that the total revenues/the total income side of this budget adds up to 877.2 million dinars approximately at that time. And if we look at the -- the more detailed income side of this budget, we do see that what I have described to you earlier today, that the original revenues/income like sales tax and -- excuse me, other kind of taxes. They are virtually nothing compared to what is listed under line 780 where it is listed "Additional funds of the Federation" in the size of 821.7 million dinars. And "additional funds of the Federation," that means money coming from the FRY. And again, that means primary emissions originating from the National Bank of Yugoslavia in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at this time, Your Honours, the Prosecution would seek to tender 65 ter 1581.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1979. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for the final exhibit that I'll show you, if we could move to tab 73 which is 65 ter 1605. Do you -- have you had an opportunity to review this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It is a decision on allocation of funds for financing the Republic of Serbian Krajina in the period January to June 1993, and it was published in the Official Gazette of the RSK on 20th April, 1993. Again, this is a budget, a plan showing the income and expenditure -- the planned income and expenditure for the RSK in this period.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention, if I may, to page 4 of the English. I believe it's page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: We may have to --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And on this page that we're now looking at, could you tell us what categories of data are relevant to your report and findings?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, what is relevant here again is the source of the income and the total -- total revenue. If we go to the bottom of this page we can see that the total revenue, meaning then the total income in this budget, adds up to 303.8-something. And we can see the income side being more detailed out. We can read on the line 781, it is stated "credits." It is there stated an amount of 2.231 going further on. And that amount, approximately, adds up to about two-thirds of the income side of this budget. And, again, bringing to your attention, "credits" in this respect means money coming from the National Bank of Yugoslavia. The primary emissions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: And it is also further stated here that under line 780 that that money is also provided directly by the FRY in the size of 609.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: 609-something --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- is that what you mean when you pause? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at this time the Prosecution would seek to tender 65 ter 1605.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P1980. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If we could refer back to that exhibit which has now been admitted as P1980, Mr. Torkildsen, did you have an additional comment to make?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. I would like to go to the expenditure side of this budget, what they are planning to use the money on.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And on what page are you?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I would be on page 6 of the translation, at the -- at the top of that page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And this would be B/C/S number 3. Are you --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. I would just like to highlight that a large part of the expenditure is going for the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you're taking that from where it says at 420?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At the -- the very first one.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. Approximately two-thirds of the budget, the income in the budget is going for the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Torkildsen, you are aware that in this case we will tender your report but we will not be relying on paragraphs 23 or paragraphs 79 to 83. And this was also done in the Milosevic and Perisic case. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And does the exclusion of those paragraphs impair your report in any way?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we would now tender the report with the exhibits, but I understand that the protocol will be that we will submit a written motion in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Indeed, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at this time I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Gosnell, cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Torkildsen.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: My name is Christopher Gosnell. I represent Mr. Hadzic in these proceedings. I am going to have a few questions for you, not too many. If any of them are not clear, please feel free to ask me for clarification and I'll do my best. How would you characterise your expertise as reflected in your report? What is the domain of your expertise?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, the domain of my expertise is that of a financial investigator with two business degrees. I know a lot about finance, having worked on financial issues for -- for 20 years plus.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what is the difference between being a financial investigator and a forensic accountant, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, I think that the main -- I work together with a lot of accountants in my -- in my current position, and I think the main difference is that financial investigators tend to get -- to get more into -- to depth regarding the issues that they are reviewing. At least certain aspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I notice from your CV that you're not an accountant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And do you think that that in any way impairs your ability to conduct the analysis that's contained in your report or you don't think that that does impair your ability to do that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I don't think that impair my ability at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And do you speak B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you read B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: As you were going through some of the documents that are footnoted in your report, and we'll look at some of them now, did you diligently ask for assistance from those who were able to speak B/C/S about stamps that appeared on some of the documents?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I -- I did -- well, during all my reviews, I asked in general for assistance from the language assistants of the -- of the OTP regarding whether it was stamps or -- or other parts of the document. I cannot only reply in general terms that I asked them about all kinds of details. I can't now - well, ten years ago - remember exactly what I asked them about, what parts of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: As you were looking at these documents, and I -- in part it seems to be suggested by your answer, were you looking closely at the form of the documents to determine in the first case authenticity but in the second case also the provenance of the documents, who exactly is responsible for issuing some of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No, did I not try to authenticate the documents. Again, back to your question regarding the stamps and so on, I did not consider whether the documents were genuine, to put it like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So you simply assumed that the documents that you were given are genuine?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what about the second part of my question, did you analyse the stamps in order to verify or ascertain the provenance; in other words, the exact issuing institution or person or body in respect of the documents?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 311, please, which is Prosecution tab 56.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were just a few moments ago shown this document. And this is now P1978. And this is the decision on appointing of signatories of the direct transfer account of the Serbian region of SBWS. And you've described it. I won't take you back through the answers you've already given. But is it the implication of Article 2 that any two of the signatories are authorised to authorise transfers from that account?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is my understanding of this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So that means transfers could be authorised without Goran Hadzic's approval or signature; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P255.253, please. That's Prosecution tab 8 for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, if you look at the B/C/S version, Mr. Torkildsen --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- you'll see there is a very, very faint stamp. We can't read it and I won't ask you any questions about it. But let me just ask you this: Do you remember seeing Goran Hadzic's signature on any document related to financial affairs after the this date, the 21st of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That I -- I simply can't remember. I reviewed many documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we could look at Article II, it talks about revenues being formed in accordance with the current legal regulations of the FRY, Republic of Serbia, and Serbian region of SBWS, whereas disbursements will be made via municipality of Beli Manastir administration. Can you explain why that is going on? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No. No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can we have P215.140, please, which is Prosecution tab 5 -- oh, I have the wrong tab number, but it is a Prosecution tab if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the exhibit number, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Yes, it is P215.140, which is 65 ter 5135.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record, this is P215.140. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Torkildsen, I just want to ask you a very general question about this document. You're familiar with it. Can you tell us in lay terms what is occurring in this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it is a document regarding the -- the expenses of the -- of the Territorial Defence training centre in -- in Erdut, and it is -- it is stated here the -- the -- the amounts it concern. It is stated here: "During a review of expenses specified as the expenditures of the Territorial Defence Special Training Centre, we found out that according to your breakdown the total expenses for December were as follows:" And the numbers are given here. And it is further stated: "Two factors participated in spending the amount of 3" -- "approximately 3.5 million dinars, the government and its ministries, and the special training centre of the Territorial Defence ... we maintain that the expenses of these two factors must be separated, which is what we did for December 1991." And then they are -- well, they are dividing these two factors as specified. And it says here that the amount for the special training centre in Erdut is an amount of 1.116.000-something dinars for the training centre. And: "We therefore kindly request from you that in the future our expenses be specified separately ..." And it's signed by Raznatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Torkildsen, that is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I was hoping for your assistance in respect of your expertise, and I'll just ask you whether you agree with me that this appears to be a signatory, Arkan, complaining about being, apparently, in his view, overcharged by the DP -- the DP Dalj farm for whatever services or goods he's been provided. Is that what's in essence happening in this letter?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, that -- that is your interpretation of -- of this document. What is stated here, that -- that these two factors must be -- must be separated, but whether it's -- can be viewed as a complaint from Arkan, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Let's leave out the word "complaint." He is suggesting to the DP Dalj farm that he has been charged too much and that he wishes to pay less. Is that what it amounts to?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, at least it amounts to that -- to say that he wants -- that his expenditures to be -- to be specified.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And reduced relative to what he's been charged; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, if it is -- if it is correct, as I take from your question, that he's been charged the whole amount and not only the amount that -- that belongs to -- to his side of this -- you are correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, we don't have all of the underlying documents as you know, so I'm not asking you this question to -- to have you verify whether or not he was or was not overcharged. All I want to verify with you is would you agree with me that this is a letter in which Arkan is saying: "I have been charged in excess of what I should have been charged, and here is the amount that I believe I should be charged"?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: At least that's one -- one -- one theory you can lead out from this document. Whether that -- that is actually the background, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, am I not -- am I misreading the document in any some way or is my reading accurate?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: What I'm saying here is that it is stated that -- that -- that he wants a separation of these two figures into one concerning the training centre in Erdut and the other part of the total amount should specify what is going to the government and the ministries.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And there is a difference between those two numbers and the number that he is proposing is less than what he's been charged. Can you agree with me that that is what the document reflects?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I can agree with you that the amount going for the training centre is less than the total amount.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, that wasn't my question. My question was: Can you agree with me that Arkan is saying that the amount that he should be paying is less than what he believes he has been charged?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, I can't agree with you on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, if we look at the letter it says there were two factors that participated in spending the amount of 3.4 million and some odd dinars, and he characterises that as your breakdown of the total expenses for December. Now, if he's referring to "your breakdown," doesn't that suggest to you that he's referring to an invoice he has received and that that's what he's being charged by DP Dalj?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it can be interpreted like that and it can be also suggested that that was the case, but I haven't seen the -- the -- underlying invoice showing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Again, that's a reasonable interpretation; correct? It's not a far-flung or biased or crazy interpretation; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it is a reasonable suggestion. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what he's suggesting there is that the actual amount that he should pay, if you look down there where it says special training centre is 1.1 million dinars. That is right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So he's talking about -- he's asking for a reduction of about 2.5 -- almost 2.5 million dinars in this letter; right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, if it is correct that he has originally received an invoice for the total amount. But, again, I haven't seen that invoice, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can you think of any reason if Arkan is being funded by the district government of the SBWS, if all of his expenses were being paid by the district government, why would he write this letter complaining about being overcharged?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, I -- I see no reason for why he should write such a letter if -- well, that -- well, considering if he has already received an invoice for the total amount. Personally, I would also have complained about an invoice of -- of whatever that did not concern me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you would complaint about that if the money was coming out of your own pocket or out of your account; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Naturally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And so from that would you infer from the basis of this letter that Arkan is somehow paying his own expenses at least as of the date of this letter, which is the 17th of January, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I'd thought in your previous question or -- or argument that you were saying that it was the year -- that it was the government of the SAO that paid for his expenses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, sir, that certainly wasn't my argument or suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see you looking at the clock and I know we need to finish at 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: But if you move to another topic, this would be a good moment, but if you still have questions about this --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No, I haven't exhausted this one, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You have not?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, I am not suggesting in any way that the government is paying his expenses as of this date. In fact, I'm suggesting the opposite. That he is complaining -- his complaint suggests that at this point he is not being funded at this point by the government. Do you understand the proposition I am putting to you?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. You are putting the proposition that -- that the government is not paying for Arkan's activities in Erdut at -- at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the basis for that is that he's complaining about his expenses, and I'm putting to you that doesn't this indicate and suggest to you, as you just said that you would complain if you are being overcharged, you would complain because the money is coming out of your pocket; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I agreed on that, but I mean it's difficult to me to be sort of further specific about this without having access to all the underlying details there in terms of invoices and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I understand that. But this document is indicative of that, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It's an indication, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, we can leave it there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Torkildsen, we take the second break a little bit earlier than what we do usually. We'll come back at 12.30. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, I was asking you before the break about inferences and I was sorry to have to ask you about inferences, but the reason I did ask you about inferences is because at paragraph 103 to 104 of your report, what you say about this document is that this document - which is still on the screen in front of us - is indicative that the district government of the SBWS was supporting Arkan. That's what you say in your report.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now that we've -- now we've -- now -- I'll give you a chance to answer. But now, we have taken a very close look at this document, wouldn't you agree with me that it seems to suggest the opposite?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: My basic understanding of this is that you have the Dalj company paying for the expenses of the Arkan training centre in Erdut and then you have the Dalj company again being reimbursed by the SAO government. That was my understanding of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we're going to come to two later documents that I think are the foundation for that view, and that's expressed in paragraphs 105 and -6 of your report and we'll get there. But just for the time being I want us to focus on the assertion that you make at 103 and 104 because at paragraph 104 you say "for instance," and then you cite this document, and you suggest that it shows that this document shows that the district government is supporting Arkan. It doesn't show that, does it? In this document it doesn't show that.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, back again to this document. This document again basically shows that the expenses should be divided into two, the training centre in Erdut and the proportion going or covering the expenses of the government and the -- and the ministries.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. That's -- that's fine. We -- obviously that interpretation is -- that may or may not be true. As you say we don't have the underlying documents. But the point being if indeed Arkan is being supported by DP Dalj, as you suggest in your report --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- it does seem a bit strange he'd be complaining about being overcharged; right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, again it can be as simple that he, Arkan, just want to pin-point that, that is the proportion of the expenses that actually is -- is -- is dedicated to the activities of the training centre. But the other part is the proportion of the expenses that relates to the government and the ministries. It's the same thing. If I can just give an example. It would be the same thing if I, for business purposes, went -- went travelling abroad and I covered all the expenses from that -- that travel, that I had two colleagues with me and I covered their expenses as well. And then when he came home to the office to have my expenses reimbursed and I would also like to sort of specify that these were not only the expenses of myself but they were also the expenses of two of my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But if the two colleagues were paying your expenses, you wouldn't care, would you?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, that is -- well, if I wouldn't care that is the difference. But at least I would have like to have it specified that these were not only the expenses for my own costs but also for my two colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P216.140, please, which is Prosecution tab 51.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'll suggest to you that this -- this is the first invoice from the DP Dalj which in any way suggests that the district government of the SBWS is supposed to pay for the expenses of the training centre. Now, do you disagree with that? I mean -- or am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I agree with that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And incidentally, the numbers just to relate this to the previous document, the invoice ends up being just a little bit lower than what Arkan is complaining about in the previous document; namely, he wants to pay 1.1 million dinars and now we have just over 1 million dinars. Do you remember that those two -- two numbers appear to at least be somewhat related?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. I can see that the amounts are approximately the same, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 05133, which is Prosecution tab 49.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is confidential Exhibit P214.140. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Torkildsen, we -- we were just looking at the invoice -- and perhaps we can even back up before that. We have Arkan's letter on the 17th of January, then we have the invoice of the 22nd of January, and now we have this document from good -- excuse me, Mr. Milanovic, and you'll notice that there is no date on this document; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That -- that is correct. At least I can't see a date now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And there is no addressee.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: There is no addressee. I mean, it -- it is a document by the -- by the Serbian district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Just commenting on you saying that there is no date on this document. That is correct. But there is actually a number on the -- on the top of this document on the left-hand side, where it is referred to number 01-73/92 and to me that indicates that this is a document from 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But we can't specify the date beyond that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the stamp there -- now, I -- unfortunately it's not translated, but I'll just put it to you that that stamp says, "SO SBWS Ministry of Defence, Vukovar." Anything in your experience of looking at documents amiss or unusual about an approval being made by the Ministry of Defence for payments?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Um --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let me new it to you specifically: Do you think that this kind of payment is one that should go through the Ministry of Finance and be approved by the Ministry of Finance, or do you think it's enough that the Ministry of Defence and the minister or the assistant minister of defence approves an expenditure of this kind?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I can't really answer that question. I wouldn't know on a detailed level who's got the -- who is able to sign off for this expense.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And I realise from one of your first answers you weren't checking these documents for authenticity, and we don't check -- we don't suggest that this document is a fake, but when you look at the form of the document now in relation to other documents that you've seen, in terms of the sums of money that are potentially involved, do you think that there is something amiss in the form of the document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm sorry, I really don't have any opinion on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, the absence of a date, the absence of an addressee, the absent of the involvement of the Ministry of Finance, the absence of approval by Goran Hadzic at least in relation to this document. Do any of those things seem out of order in relation to other similar documents that you've reviewed?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, I do agree with you that it is a bit odd that the document do not contain a date, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Can we have P149, please, which is Prosecution tab 57.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this document is not referred to in your report, but it is one of the additional documents that you have looked at. And -- well, first of all, let me just ask you: Looking at that front page, do you remember the document in its entirety? Can you recall what that document looks like?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No, I don't. It was more than ten years ago since I reviewed these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. Well, in that case we're going to have to do a bit of a page turning exercise I'm afraid. This first page appears to be some handwritten notes.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we see that there is a signature there on the front which has otherwise been authenticated before this Trial Chamber as Mr. Milanovic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now if we can turn the page, please, and go to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We see an invoice for something called -- identified as ski trousers. And the account number is to a military post, BR-5530-50. Does that in any way ring a bell, that number, that identification?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Specifically which number are you pointing at?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, it's -- you see in the left-hand box there at the top under account number 249?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And there is a reference to a military post, BR-5530-50?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No, I do not relate that to anything specific, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: In your work as a financial investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor, have you ever examined JNA or SSNO accounts?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Not -- not that I would call regular accounts in terms of if you are referring to bank statements or -- or accounts at a detailed level. The accounts that I had access to are typically the -- the accounts and the budgets that -- that we had examples of earlier today. It -- it was never at such a detailed level.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I didn't mean to limit my question so specifically. Have you in your work in general examined how the JNA or the SSNO or other federal military agencies engaged in expenditures?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, just at the aggregate level and not at the detailed level, because I never had access to the detailed accounts of the JNA, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. We can turn through the next one, two, three, four, five -- six pages. And those are all in similar form. They appear to be invoices from this company called "Working Women," and there are various accounts listed there in addition to the military post we just referred to. There is the Tenje TO, one is blank, and there is one that says SAO SBWS government bureau Belgrade. And then we get to this last or this --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we can go to the third last page, please. Yeah, sorry, I'm sorry. I'm looking for the third last page which should be page 8. That's it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this social bookkeeping service slip, is that the SDK that you refer to in your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is that -- is that some kind of a record of a payment out of the account?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It seems like that, that this is a record of a payment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, have you seen other similar slips in the course of your investigations?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Again, I'm -- well, most likely, but I'm -- I just can't remember details about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, did you conduct any investigations at all at the SDK or did you receive -- let me put it a different way: Did you receive documents from the SDK as part of your work --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No, I did not have access to the detailed accounts of the SDK, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we could please go to the next page of the document. It appears to be a summary of the foregoing receipts. We won't linger over this. If we could just turn the page, please, to the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I know you don't read B/C/S but I put it to you that that stamp there is from the Ministry of Finance of the district government of the SBWS, and what you have there is a typewritten indication of Goran Hadzic's name but he hasn't signed it. Would you agree that that -- and also on the top there on the right-hand side it says Ministry of Finance of the Serb region of SBWS. Would you agree with me that what appears to be happening here is that the Ministry of Finance is preparing this authorisation form for Mr. Hadzic's signature, he hasn't signed it, but this is part of the process of paying the foregoing invoices that we've seen in previous pages?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, your question seems logical to me. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to how these pages were bundled together into a single document? That's how we've received them, and I am wondering whether you have any knowledge as to how this was bundled together?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No, I don't. As I said earlier today, I only reviewed the documents that were already collected by -- by others and entered into the evidence system of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And now that you've looked at this document and the -- the amount is 772.000 dinars, does it strike you as even more anomalous, the previous document, signed by Mr. Milanovic with no date, no addressee, and no authorisation from the Ministry of Finance?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, I do agree you that -- that -- that normally documents like this should have a date on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And judging by --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Whether this is just a draft that was not finalised, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, sir, just to be clear about the point I'm making to you. I mean, here we have an authorisation for 772.000 dinars, a few invoices from a clothing company, apparently, and the Ministry of Finance, apparently, has drafted this authorisation letter for Mr. Hadzic's signature. The previous document, the one signed by Mr. Milanovic, there is no date, there is no letter by the Ministry of Finance, there is no addressee, there is no authorisation from Mr. Hadzic. When you compare these two documents, wouldn't you agree that the Milanovic document appears anomalous in terms of the procedure for authorising payments?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, authorising payments should have had the signatures and dates on it. That would be -- that would be normal, yes. But what was normal in that region at the time, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, this document indicates what the normal procedure, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, unless this is a draft and the -- and date would have been put into the final document and the final document would have a signature as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I hate to belabour this. I don't have any problem with there being no date on this --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: On this last page. All I'm suggesting is that someone has gone to the trouble, even for the some of 772.000 dinars, someone from the Ministry of Finance has gone to the trouble of drafting an authorisation letter for Mr. Hadzic. No such letter is appended to Mr. Milanovic's letter which presumably would involve a larger sum; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Could be. I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 01017, please, Prosecution tab 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This is a document, sir, that is mentioned in your report. I believe we may have discussed earlier today.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yup.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: You see it's from the SSNO logistics assistant who is a General-Colonel Vladan Sljivic and it's dated the 7th of April, 1992, and he's sending this document to the commanders of the 1st and 2nd Military Area as well as the RSK Main Staff in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now could we please turn the page in English and go to item 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: "All the expenses of unit preparations and relocation are to be included into one-year plan for financing of the units. In accordance with the schematics for logistics bases and reliance of the Territorial Defence units on logistic bases of the military zone, development planning and finance management will ensure that the financial needs of the TO units on the territory of RS Krajina are covered." Do you have any knowledge about these one-year plans for financing the units? Did you ever look into whether or not the SSNO or JNA were preparing such plans?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: As I stated earlier today, I don't have -- I never seen the -- the detailed planning of this. We have had examples from the documents earlier today when they were referring to a planned quota, et cetera, and so on, but I never seen the detailed planning behind this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge from any source at all in the course of your work with the Office of the Prosecutor that the SSNO or the JNA or for that matter the Republic of Serbia, Ministry of Defence, which isn't covered by this document, just to be clear, but from any of those sources have you seen any indication that any of those entities were providing direct support to TO units in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, again, yes -- yes, we do have in terms of the requests from -- from the RSK or the SAO that were going to the Serbian Ministry of Defence and the -- and outcome of that. Again, that was discussed in the -- in the exhibits that we looked at -- at earlier today. But again, as I've said, I never had access to the -- to the detailed accounts of the JNA, the RSK, or the SAO at a very detailed level. It was just at the aggregate level.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: My question was whether or not there was direct support to TO units in Croatia; in other words, not through the district governments. Because as I read this document, there appears to be an implication that the SSNO has somehow prepared plans for financial support for TO units. And so that's what I was wondering about when I asked that question, whether you saw any evidence that there was direct support to TO units in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, one of the documents involving the Serbian Ministry of Defence that we looked at this morning suggests that there were direct financial assistance from the Republic of Serbia to the TO Defence. That is correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06155, please, which is P1975. And that's Prosecution tab 75.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sir, these are the shorthand notes of the Supreme Defence Council dated the 2nd of June, 1993. You looked at this document earlier today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 12, please, in the English. And in the B/C/S it's under item 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And about halfway down the page, this is Zivota Panic speaking. And he says: "As to the army, we have had the livestock farms, the farms, we were involved in public labour before, and we still have it. If this had not been the case, the pressure on the Government regarding the money would have been much bigger than it is now. We used to have a large income. But now no one is demanding such labour, because they do not have the money and they cannot pay for it." It seems as if the JNA is involved in agra business. Do you know anything about the JNA being involved in commercial enterprises or co-operative enterprise or any commercial activity?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That's -- that's a difficult question for me -- for me to answer. I have reviewed thousands of pages of documents, but I can't remember the details regarding this, so it's difficult for me to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's fair enough, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have L35, please. Yeah, that's Prosecution tab 60 for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is the -- or purports to be the budget of the Serb region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem for the year 1991. And it appears to have been adopted by the Assembly on the 8th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we can just turn the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And first of all, I should ask you: Do you recall this document from your preparation for today?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I've reviewed this document. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And how would you rate it from the point of view of being a budget that actually reflects professional preparation? Is it -- is it a professional document or would you say it's a bunch of numbers that have been more or less arbitrarily slapped on paper by someone?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No, it seems to be a professional budget. What -- what is different from -- from this budget compared to other budgets is that this was early in time, meaning 1991 where the financing through -- through primary issues had to a large extent had just started. So we will see from this budget that you do have a -- also a lot of -- what I determine to be original income in this budget, like -- like taxes, VAT, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Is it normal that a budget would be produced in the second-to-last month of that year?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is not normal under normal circumstances, but these circumstances in that region at that time were not normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. Based on your knowledge of the situation and the documents you've seen, do you think it's a remotely accurate number to say that 16.000 million dinars of sales tax was collected in 1991 by the district government?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, simply, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P208.140, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Other than your work here at the Tribunal, have you any experience at all in dealing with financial investigations into transfers between states? Financial transfers between states.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do. Most of the -- well, not most, but many of the big financial investigations I've been doing has been about money crossing borders, so I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And does that include examining documents written at the highest level by state leaders, state leadership, ministers, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No, it has very much been work at the much more detailed and lower level in terms of bank transactions going from bank A in country to bank B in another country.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Okay. Then I'll pose my next question and ask you to rely on your experience from the Tribunal. This is a letter written by Minister Milan Martic directly, apparently, to Mr. Milosevic. Is it normal that a letter about financial affairs is being sent directly by a minister to the president of another country?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Whether that is normal or not, I -- I wouldn't know. I guess this depends on the -- on, well, most likely whatever personal relationship it was between Mr. Martic and Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Those are my questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Biersay, redirect?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: No redirect, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, this brings your testimony to an end. We thank you very much for coming to The Hague to assist the Tribunal. You are now released as a witness. The Court Usher will escort you out of the court and we wish you a safe journey home. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, do we have another witness ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next witness arrived yesterday afternoon and we are not prepared to begin his testimony today. I do know that there is an outstanding issue for the Chamber with respect to an aspect of this witness's testimony, an urgent motion was filed yesterday to which the Prosecution has at noon today filed its response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So that is an outstanding issue that may affect the examination or cross. There was one other issue that I would like to raise with the Chamber not related to these witnesses, but since we have a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I think to do it, we'd ask to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Court adjourned.
